header:
Date: 2026-12-02
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Park (Redwood SE), Olivia Reyes (Redwood CSM), Samantha Ortiz (CISO, Northshore), Daniel Reed (Head of Platform), Priya Kapoor (Security Engineer), Ethan Cole (DevOps), Jared Lim (PM)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're on for our weekly security sync with Northshore, we did a quick roll call.
[00:08] Samantha (Northshore CISO): Hi all, Sam here.
[00:11] Daniel (Platform): Daniel, hey.
[00:13] Liam (Redwood SE): Liam here. Quick note, I might share my screen when we get into the audit logs.
[00:18] Priya (Security Eng): Priya.
[00:20] Ethan (DevOps): Ethan, yes.
[00:22] Jared (PM): Jared.
[00:24] Maya: Great. Quick agenda: SSO status, audit logs/format, data retention and PII handling, SOC2 artifacts, any blockers. We'll go through items and recap next steps.
[00:34] Samantha: Sounds good. We had a blocker on SSO last week — our IdP team made a config change, so wanted to confirm what you need from us.
[00:40] Maya: Right, thanks. On our side we supported the SAML metadata you sent, we had one attribute mapping mismatch — your IdP sends 'employee_id' as 'empId' — that caused the initial mapping to fail. We patched a temporary mapping in the pilot tenant, but for production we recommend canonical attributes.
[00:55] Priya: Yeah, we saw that. Also, do you support SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows, and can you enforce SAML signing requirements?
[01:04] Liam: We support both; SP-initiated and IdP-initiated. We also require signed assertions for the production integration. In the pilot tenant we accept unsigned for quicker testing but flagged that as a deviation.
[01:15] Samantha: Ok that's fine for pilot but we'll need signed assertions for go-live. Also need SCIM for group sync — is that in scope?
[01:22] Olivia (CSM): We can enable SCIM for groups, it's part of the enterprise integration. I'll add that to the rollout checklist.
[01:28] Daniel: Great. Next, audit logs. We tried ingesting your sample audit logs into our ELK stack and had some field mismatches. Liam, can you walk through what you ship?
[01:37] Liam: Sure, I'll share my screen. 
[01:40] [01:40] Liam (screen share): Ok, so the audit payload is JSON lines, one event per line. Key fields: timestamp, request_id, user_id (or anon_user_id for masked requests), route, model_name, tokens_in, tokens_out, lat_ms, and an event_type field. We also include a hashed user identifier for privacy.
[01:58] Priya: We noticed a 'sessionHash' field in the sample that didn't match our parse rules, it ended up in message.body in our ingestion.
[02:05] Liam: Right — so that's the hash of the kv-cache session, we call it 'sessionHash'. It was labelled inconsistently in an earlier export, sorry about that — we pushed a fix this morning to unify on 'session_id'. If you can re-run ingestion with the latest sample it should map correctly.
[02:19] Ethan: Also, are PII fields ever present in logs? We need to ensure nothing like account numbers or SSNs make it into the logs.
[02:27] Liam: Good question. By default we mask obvious PII from generated outputs in hosted pilot: we apply regex-based masking for patterns matching account numbers, SSNs, emails when configured. We also strongly encourage customers to provide a PII regex list so our masking covers your in-house formats. For the POC we masked email addresses and account-like patterns in textual outputs; request/response bodies in raw logs are redacted for stored logs but we do have configurable retention for raw event blobs if the customer opts in.
[02:53] Priya: We need confirmation that the raw audit events stored for the pilot don't contain customer PII and that the hash is one-way and salted. Also what's your KMS model?
[03:04] Maya: Redwood supports both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM. For the POC you were on Redwood-managed, which is AES-256 at rest. If you require CMK, we can switch to a dedicated KMS key in your cloud account for encrypting at rest. The session hashes are HMAC-SHA256 with per-tenant salt — the salt is rotated periodically and we can provide detail in the crypto spec doc.
[03:25] Samantha: That's good. We will likely want CMK for production. For the pilot it's ok to remain managed but need evidence in the SOC2 bucket.
[03:33] Maya: We'll attach the SOC2 Type II report and pen test summary after the call.
[03:36] Olivia: I'll drop the docs in the shared drive and also send a secure link.
[03:40] Daniel: On retention, Priya, we need 7 years for some logs per compliance; realistically we might tier hot vs cold. What retention options can you support?
[03:50] Liam: We support configurable retention per event type. By default audit events retained 90 days in hot storage, 1 year in warm; we can export to the customer's S3 for long-term retention or configure a cold archive for 7+ years. For hosted customers we provide an automated export job to your S3, encrypted with your CMK if requested.
[04:07] Priya: And for the pilot, is export enabled by default?
[04:10] Maya: Not by default — we can enable an export connector for your pilot tenant. That would route logs daily to your S3 bucket; we can provide an IAM policy example.
[04:19] Ethan: We'll need that IAM policy, yes. Also want to confirm the log format for ingestion — field names matter.
[04:24] Liam: I'll send the latest schema and ELK mapping. Example field names: @timestamp, request_id, user_hash, session_id, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, latency_ms, event_type, route.
[04:37] Jared: Quick question on data residency — our law team requires EU data residency for certain customers. Does your hosted pilot guarantee region pinning?
[04:45] Maya: For the hosted pilot we pinned workloads to eu-west-1 for your EU pilot traffic. For production we offer region pinning and private deployments for stricter residency, including VPC connectors.
[04:55] Samantha: And for private deployment, does the control plane still touch metadata? We want a fully air-gapped option for high-risk lines of business.
[05:02] Liam: Full private deploy (on-prem) option is available; in that configuration the control plane is customer-managed and Redwood provides an appliance and deployment scripts. For VPC-private, the control plane still has a small management channel but can be configured to route through your proxy. We'll follow up with the deployment model doc.
[05:18] Priya: Ok. Another compliance detail — audit logs need to be immutable and tamper-evident for some audits. Do you support write-once storage or append-only logs?
[05:27] Liam: We can configure immutability by exporting logs to S3 with Object Lock enabled (governance or compliance mode) and we also support streaming logs to your SIEM which can enforce retention and immutability controls.
[05:38] Samantha: About SOC2 scoping — will the Type II report cover the hosting environment used for the pilot?
[05:44] Maya: Yes, our SOC2 Type II covers production hosting environment; we will annotate the report to show which environment maps to your pilot tenant. There is also a complementary pen test summary with remediation notes.
[05:55] Priya: Do you have any open high-severity findings in the last test? We need to know before go-live planning.
[06:01] Maya: The latest summary shows no open high severity items; a couple of medium issues were remediated with config changes last quarter — we'll include the remediation timeline.
[06:10] Daniel: Let's talk about credentials and token handling — how are tokens rotated and do you support short-lived service tokens for our automation?
[06:18] Liam: We support short-lived tokens via our Token Service; you can issue tokens that expire in as little as 15 minutes. Service principals can be scoped to specific routes. We also support OAuth2 client credentials for automation and can rotate secrets with your KMS.
[06:30] Ethan: For the pilot we'll need an automation token with limited scope to run benchmark jobs. Does revocation propagate quickly?
[06:36] Liam: Revocation is immediate — our auth layer checks token revocation and caches for a short TTL (under 10 seconds) so you shouldn't see extended access.
[06:44] Priya: About telemetry — do you capture prompt text in traces? For compliance we prefer prompts to be hashed before being sent to observability tooling.
[06:53] Liam: Observability traces include a request_id and a hashed prompt by default. Full prompt storage is optional and only enabled if you opt in for debugging; by default we store only metadata and sanitized snippets.
[07:05] Samantha: Good. On masking, can you show an example of how an account number is redacted in the logs?
[07:11] Liam: Sure, example: original output 'Account 123456789' becomes 'Account [REDACTED-ACC-xxxxxx]'. The hash suffix allows linking across events without exposing full value.
[07:23] Priya: That should work but we need the regex list for our regional account numbers — sending that after the call.
[07:29] Maya: Perfect. Now a quick note on model choices: we noticed latency/cost tradeoffs during the last benchmark — Redwood suggested a quantized variant for chat that reduced cost by ~35% with small quality delta. Any security implications there?
[07:41] Liam: No security change from quantization itself; it's purely a runtime/kernel choice. The only operational implication is a different model artifact to manage. For compliance you still get same audit trails.
[07:51] Daniel: For POC results review, can we get a CSV of per-request latencies and tokens so we can run our own cost models?
[07:57] Olivia: Yes, we can export a CSV of the pilot window; I'll coordinate with Liam on schema and will share via secure link.
[08:05] Samantha: Ok good. Any remaining blockers on SSO or logs?
[08:08] Priya: From security side we need the schemata, SOC2 docs, and confirmation of CMK option. Also would like the exact hash algorithm details.
[08:16] Maya: We'll provide the crypto spec and KMS options. Liam will send the log schema and ELK mapping; Olivia will share docs.
[08:24] Maya: Recap of next steps: Maya to send SOC2 and pen test; Liam to send audit schema and ELK mappings and example IAM policy; Priya to send retention matrix and PII regex list; Olivia to set up SCIM enablement ticket and share export link for CSV.
[08:39] Daniel: Sounds good. Can we pencil a 30-minute follow-up next Tuesday to verify the log ingestion after you send the new sample?
[08:46] Maya: Yes we can do Tuesday 14:00 — I'll send the invite.
[08:50] Samantha: Thanks everyone.
[08:52] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up.
[08:54] [END]
